strings: Shadow Priest Sarvis stands inside the ruined chapel of Deathknell, serving as one of the primary guides for newly awakened Forsaken. He introduces fresh corpses to their grim reality, directing them to purge mindless undead and gather intelligence on local threats. Under Lady Sylvanas's banner, Sarvis works tirelessly to shape bewildered undead into disciplined servants of the Forsaken.

Within the shadowy chapel of Deathknell, Shadow Priest Sarvis waits for those who have just clawed their way out of the grave. The awakening of a Forsaken soul is jarring and horrific, with many immediately losing their minds to mindless frenzy or despondency. Sarvis acts as an anchor, giving purpose to the newly risen. He assigns new recruits to put down the shambling, mindless corpses roaming the cemetery and directs them to secure Deathknell's borders against the encroaching Scourge.

Beyond acclimating new recruits, Sarvis oversees crucial local defenses against lingering threats in Tirisfal Glades. He coordinates the containment of Scourge forces probing Deathknell's perimeter. By directing novices toward vital intelligence and martial trials, Sarvis ensures that the town remains a fortified bastion for the Forsaken.

Shandris Feathermoon is the General of the Sentinel Army and the adopted daughter of Tyrande Whisperwind and Malfurion Stormrage. A veteran archer of the War of the Ancients, she now commands night elf military forces throughout Kalimdor from Feathermoon Stronghold on Sardor Isle off the coast of Feralas.

Ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients, the demonic Burning Legion destroyed the village of Ara-Hinam, separating a young Shandris from her family. Fleeing south, she was rescued by Kur'talos Ravencrest's forces and adopted by the Priestess of the Moon, Tyrande Whisperwind. Though initially forbidden from the battlefield, Shandris covertly shadowed the Sisters of Elune, proving herself an exceptional markswoman. When the satyr Xavius assaulted Malfurion Stormrage, Shandris struck the fiend with an arrow from the treeline, providing the opening Malfurion needed to entangle and neutralize the traitor.

Following the Great Sundering and the founding of the Sentinels, Shandris became an indispensable commander within the night elf military. Centuries later in the War of the Satyr, she led squads into brutal skirmishes against lingering demonic remnants, witnessing firsthand the tragic unleashed fury of the earliest worgen. During the Third War, Shandris led the Shadowleaves sentinels alongside Tyrande, standing upon the slopes of Mount Hyjal to defend the World Tree Nordrassil against Archimonde's legions.

Today, General Feathermoon serves as the supreme field commander of the Sentinel army. Stationed on Sardor Isle, she oversees Feathermoon Stronghold, an imposing elven fortress that keeps watch over the primal wilds of Feralas. From this island outpost, she monitors the encroaching threats of savage gnolls, lingering Gordunni ogres, hate-fueled satyrs, and the expanding power of the Horde in southern Kalimdor.

Shenthul is a jungle troll rogue trainer based in the shadowy subterranean reaches of the Cleft of Shadow in Orgrimmar. As an operative of the Shattered Hand, he orchestrates espionage operations across Kalimdor and initiates rising rogues into the guild's covert ranks.

Tucked away inside the murky depths of the Cleft of Shadow, Shenthul serves as one of the Horde's foremost rogue mentors. While the warriors and shamans above march openly across the red dust of Durotar, Shenthul trains those who prefer stealth, ambush, and subterfuge. Under his tutelage, initiates master essential fieldcraft and lethal arts, learning to operate within the unforgiving politics and harsh wilderness of Kalimdor.

Shenthul represents the Shattered Hand, an order transformed from an old orcish clan into the Horde's intelligence network and secret service. He views the organization as a timeless, watchful veil blanketing Kalimdor—acting as investigator, judge, jury, and executioner. Fiercely pragmatic and independent of shifting political tides, Shenthul famously reminds outsiders that the Shattered Hand existed long before Warchief Thrall took power and will endure long after him.

Beyond basic training, Shenthul coordinates delicate missions into contested territories. His assignments send operatives on perilous infiltration assignments, such as conducting deep-cover operations against hostile interests, practicing their lockpicking on the Venture Company's locked supply boxes around Windshear Crag, and testing recruits through demanding clandestine trials. When poisons strike his field agents, Shenthul ensures they secure remedies before fatal consequences take hold.

Shoni the Shilent is an industrious gnome engineer stationed in Stormwind City's bustling Dwarven District. As commander of the Gnomeregan underground assault crew, she directs Alliance adventurers into the Deadmines to salvage the power supply of a goblin shredder, fuel for the machines she hopes will break a path back into Gnomeregan.

Operating out of the smoky workshops of the Dwarven District, Shoni represents gnomish strategic ingenuity far from the lost halls of Gnomeregan. Her engineering plans are ambitious. With Gnomeregan in the hands of the troggs, Shoni is organizing an underground assault to retake it, and she sends operatives into the subterranean tunnels beneath Westfall for the parts her crew needs.

Shoni's plan rests on the gnomes' own gyrodrillmatic excavationators, heavy drilling machines meant to break through the rocky underground borders of Gnomeregan and open the way for a gnomish assault. They lack the power to do it, so she wants the intact power supply, the Gnoam Sprecklesprocket, from a working goblin shredder deep in the Deadmines. Later, she also sends adventurers into Gnomeregan itself to tear apart its robots for spare parts to repair her fleet.

Thrall is the Warchief of the Horde and the ruler of Durotar, holding court from the Valley of Wisdom in Orgrimmar. Once a human slave raised to be an arena gladiator, he broke the chains of his people, rediscovered their ancient shamanic traditions, and led them across the Great Sea to build a new homeland.

Born Go'el, the son of Frostwolf chieftain Durotan and Draka, Thrall was orphaned as an infant when his parents were murdered by Gul'dan's assassins. He was discovered by human commander Aedelas Blackmoore, who named him 'Thrall'—meaning slave—and raised him at Durnholde Keep as an arena fighter with an education in human tactics. Aided by his foster sister Taretha Foxton, Thrall eventually escaped his captors. Guided by the Frostwolf exile Drek'Thar, he cast aside demonic corruption to master the elemental spirits, becoming the first of a new generation of orcish shaman.

Thrall joined forces with the legendary Orgrim Doomhammer to liberate the lethargic orcs languishing in Alliance internment camps after the Second War. When Doomhammer fell in battle, he bestowed his black plate armor and mighty warhammer upon Thrall, naming him the new Warchief. Following prophetic visions from the mysterious Prophet Medivh, Thrall led his people to commandeer human ships and sail across the Great Sea to the forgotten continent of Kalimdor, escaping the doom falling upon the Eastern Kingdoms.

In Kalimdor, Thrall reshaped the Horde from a warmongering engine into an alliance of survival and honor. He rescued the Darkspear trolls led by Vol'jin and allied with Cairne Bloodhoof's tauren before leading the coalition alongside human and night elf forces to defeat the Burning Legion atop Mount Hyjal. Afterward, Thrall founded the nation of Durotar and its capital Orgrimmar, named after his father and mentor. Despite maintaining an uneasy peace with Jaina Proudmoore's Theramore, Thrall now balances the defense of his fragile nation with controversial alliances, such as admitting the Forsaken of Lordaeron into the Horde fold.

Prince Thunderaan is the ancient Prince of Air, a colossal elemental struck down and betrayed during the ancient wars between fire and wind. Consumed in part by Ragnaros the Firelord, his remnant essence was sealed into shattered bindings entrusted to the Firelord's lieutenants. Long ago, during the Elemental Sundering—a five-thousand-year clash fought between the forces of fire and air deep within Azeroth—Ragnaros sought to destroy and consume Thunderaan. Unable to entirely devour the Prince of Air, Ragnaros sealed what little remained of Thunderaan's essence inside a talisman of elemental binding. To prevent the Prince from ever reforming, the Firelord shattered the talisman into two flawless halves. He entrusted one piece to Baron Geddon and the other to Garr, hiding both within the volcanic depths of the Molten Core beneath Blackrock Mountain.

Those daring enough to invade the Molten Core can wrench both halves of the binding from Ragnaros's lieutenants. Tyrande Whisperwind is the High Priestess of Elune and the supreme leader of the night elves. Alongside her beloved, the Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage, she guided her people through the cataclysmic War of the Ancients and ten millennia of the Long Vigil. Now governing from the sacred boughs of Teldrassil, she commands the Sisterhood of Elune and directs the Sentinel army in defense of Kalimdor's sacred wilderness.

Born in the ancient city of Suramar, Tyrande grew up alongside the twin brothers Malfurion and Illidan Stormrage. While the brothers followed druidism and sorcery, Tyrande entered the service of Elune as a novice in the sisterhood. When the demonic Burning Legion first invaded Azeroth during the War of the Ancients, the dying High Priestess Dejahna chose Tyrande as her successor. Blessed with direct favor from the Moon Goddess, Tyrande transformed the Sisterhood into a radiant fighting force, wielding both divine restoration and searing lunar wrath to deliver her people from the brink of total annihilation.
The Long Vigil and the Sentinels

Following the Great Sundering and the sealing of the Well of Eternity, Malfurion and the druids entered the Emerald Dream for deep, prolonged hibernations. Tyrande took upon herself the lonely burden of defending their recovering realm. She organized the Sentinels—an elite cadre of warrior-women who patrolled Kalimdor's forests for ten thousand years. Throughout this Long Vigil, she stood watchful guard over ancient evils and lingering demonic remnants, maintaining unbroken faith in Elune while she waited centuries between brief reunions with Malfurion.
